Seems to me like almost the living definition of "Emergent Properties"... In this case it seem that quite a number of each of the "building blocks" (or even sets of them) do nothing by themselves; but when all added together; the effects of the whole is greater then the sum of each part.

Very thought provoking on how little we really know about how complex systems actually work!

Very insightful observation about emergence. The general public is under the impression that cell biology and origin are well understood by scientists. But this is far from true. Biology still has no theory of how the first cell actually emerged. To put the problem simply:

The first cell had to have a subsystem for eating and subsystem for self-replicating. A cell with one but not the other cannot live. Both of those subsystems are very complicated. So how could each of them have evolved without the other one? But for both of them to suddenly appear in one cell is essentially impossible in terms of probabilities.
